reframing_when: The question addresses a symptom or proximate cause without asking why that symptom exists — one why isn't enough.
The question has settled on a specific formulation ('how do we fix X?') without verifying that X is the root cause rather than a surface manifestation.
The question ends at an unexamined assertion or organizational assumption rather than a falsifiable fact — the chain of 'why' stopped at cultural myth instead of a first principle.
The question is about treating a recurring problem that keeps returning because the root cause has never been identified.
reframing_move: Ask 'why?' repeatedly until the question shifts from the presenting symptom to the underlying cause: 'why is X happening?' leads to 'why is Y happening?' which eventually reveals that the real question isn't about X at all, but about Z — a deeper structural issue the surface question cannot see.
curation_note: Five whys operates directly on question structure by converting surface questions into deeper ones. The source is explicit: the method exists to 'separate reliable knowledge from assumption' and to reach first principles. It is a pure question-transformation tool — the output of five whys is a better question, not an answer.

reframing_when.note: All four activations grounded: proximate vs root cause (core definition), premature formulation (clarity tip usage), myth vs first principle (hitting a first principle), and recurring problems (preventing recurrence).

frame_patterns_challenged.note: Symptom as problem is the primary target — the question addresses the symptom, not the disease. Premature intellectualization: the question jumped to a specific formulation without observing the deeper structure.
